title: The diagonal of a smooth morphism is Koszul regular and perfect
statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let f:X\to S be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] whose diagonal is a closed immersion (that is, f is separated) and whose pure relative dimension is d. Then the diagonal \Delta:X\to X\times_S X [def-pc-base-change] is a Koszul-regular immersion of codimension d, meaning that locally its defining ideal is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. In particular \Delta is a perfect immersion, meaning that \Delta_*\mathcal O_X is locally a perfect complex over X\times_S X [def-pc-perfect-complex]; since X and S are Noetherian, \Delta is also proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tags 067U (smooth diagonal is Koszul regular) and 068C (perfect and proper immersion consequences)

proof.text: By the cited smooth-diagonal statement [lem-sc-smooth-diagonal-regular-immersion], applied to f (smooth, diagonal a closed immersion, pure relative dimension d), every point of X\times_S X has an affine open neighbourhood U=\operatorname{Spec}A on which the ideal of \Delta is A or is generated by an A-regular sequence of length d.

On each such affine neighbourhood the ideal of \Delta is generated by an A-regular sequence of length d (or is A, generated by the empty sequence). The cited regular-sequence lemma [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] says that every regular sequence in A is Koszul-regular. Therefore locally the ideal of \Delta is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence of length d: \Delta is a Koszul-regular immersion of codimension d.

X\times_S X is of finite type over the Noetherian scheme S, hence Noetherian, and \Delta is a closed immersion. By Step 2 every point of X\times_S X has an affine open neighbourhood on which the ideal of \Delta is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence, which is the hypothesis of the cited statement [lem-sc-koszul-regular-closed-immersion-perfect] with Y=X\times_S X. It gives that \Delta_*\mathcal O_X is locally perfect on X\times_S X.

The diagonal is a closed immersion by the separatedness hypothesis. A closed immersion is separated, of finite type, and universally closed; hence it is proper. The source and target are Noetherian by the hypotheses, so this gives the stated properness conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_diagonal_koszul_regular_perfect_proper {X S : Scheme.{u}} (d : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ S) [IsNoetherian S] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsClosedImmersion (pullback.diagonal f)] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (pullback f f).toRingedSpace))] [∀ U : (pullback f f).Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings (pullback f f).toRingedSpace).over U))] : (∀ y : (pullback f f : Scheme.{u}), ∃ U : (pullback f f).Opens, y ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∃ (I : Ideal (Γ(pullback f f, U))) (r : ℕ) (g : Fin r → Γ(pullback f f, U)), I = Ideal.span (Set.range g) ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular g ∧ (∃ e : Scheme.Opens.toScheme ((pullback.diagonal f) ⁻¹ᵁ U) ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of (Γ(pullback f f, U) ⧸ I)), (pullback.diagonal f) ∣_ U ≫ U.toSpecΓ = e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) ∧ (I = ⊤ ∨ r = d)) ∧ Scheme.IsPerfect (pullback f f) ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (pullback f f).toRingedSpace)) 0).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.diagonal f)).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))) ∧ IsProper (pullback.diagonal f)
